children: Capital has its own people map.

Nostr is built by developers, designers, relay operators, writers and communities. It also needs donors, grant makers, Bitcoin-native funds and investors who understand when a public protocol needs patient money. These eight profiles separate direct Nostr grants from human-rights funding, Bitcoin venture capital and broader frontier capital.
The grant desk that made Nostr feel fundable
Start with OpenSats when you want the direct grant trail: who received support, what kind of Nostr work was funded and why open-source infrastructure needs a public runway.

children: Human Rights Foundation Bitcoin Development Fund
The human-rights lens on censorship-resistant communication
Use HRF when you want to understand Nostr as freedom technology, not only as a social app or builder scene.
The seed-stage lane for Bitcoin-native experiments
Use Bitcoin Frontier Fund as the startup lens: not a public Nostr grant desk, but a Bitcoin-native early-stage investor to watch when a Nostr project becomes a venture-backed product.
Bitcoin-only capital that already knows the Nostr room
Use Ten31 when the question is how a Nostr company fits inside Bitcoin-first capital rather than generic crypto venture.
Direct Nostr thesis in freedom-tech language
The Bitcoin-only Series A lane with a Nostr-aware edge
Use ego death capital for the harder commercial question: when does a Nostr idea become a real Bitcoin business?
Nostr-adjacent through Bitcoin companies and advisors
The category builder for Bitcoin-native venture
Use TVP to understand the institutional Bitcoin-native venture lens around infrastructure, Lightning, media and startup categories that Nostr companies may enter.
The Lightning investor near Nostr's payment edge
Use Fulgur when Nostr turns into wallets, zaps, Lightning infrastructure, payments and the harder payment UX underneath the social layer.
Nostr-adjacent through Lightning, wallets and Nostr-connected portfolio work
The broad venture lane if Nostr becomes a global startup story
Use Draper Associates as the broad venture reference: not a Nostr grant rail, but a possible future lane for venture-scale decentralized infrastructure companies.

children: The human map works when it shows pressure.
Names become useful when the reader can see what pressure surrounds them: code, money, moderation, media, events, migration, trust and the rooms where the community argues itself into shape.
The community starts with keys and relays, but it becomes readable through the people who build, host, argue, explain and show up.
Nostr survives through maintenance: NIPs, clients, libraries, signers, relays, wallets and the people who keep them usable.
Hosts, writers, musicians, video makers, journalists and educators make the protocol legible to people outside the builder circle.
Conferences, meetups, live streams, Nests and recordings show where the scene becomes more than a feed.
Zaps, grants, paid infrastructure, moderation tools and trust systems reveal what the community values and where it still fights.
